root.name: Italian Game: Rosentreter Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. d4

overview: White plays 4.d4 at once, offering a pawn for the centre and open lines against the Giuoco Piano set-up. Black can take with 4...exd4 or 4...Bxd4, and White hopes for a quick development with O-O, c3 and e5 along with pressure on f7. I am not sure of the best lines, but accurate defence appears to leave Black comfortable, as with the Scotch Gambit family.

white_ideas.idea: Open the centre with d4, then play O-O or Ng5/Bxf7 ideas for an attack.
Use the c4 bishop on the f7 diagonal and develop quickly.

black_ideas.idea: Take on d4, return the pawn or retreat with ...Bb6 and develop ...Nf6 and ...d6.
Neutralise the pin on f7 and consolidate.

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after the d-pawn exchange, with White a pawn down for development.

character.notes: Sacrificial and open; both sides can go wrong with tactics around f7 and d4.

gambit.notes: Black can take on d4 and keep the pawn for a time, though tactical lines may make it hard.

soundness.notes: Considered inferior to the Evans Gambit and Scotch lines; likely dubious for White but I am unsure.

structure.notes: Open lines after the central pawns are exchanged.

approach.notes: A rare gambit, seldom seen among strong players.

level.notes: Needs concrete knowledge of the tactics; unsound lines are not beginner.

sublines_that_differ.name: 4...Bxd4
sublines_that_differ.how: White gives more material for a king hunt.

character.reason: White gambits for open lines and an attack on f7.

gambit.reason: White offers the d-pawn for development.

soundness.reason: A rarely played gambit that Black can probably meet comfortably.

structure.reason: Central pawns come off and lines are open.

level.reason: A dubious gambit is never beginner.

plans.reason: White's bishop on c4 and quick development aim at f7.
